subject: Request: Timebound retention carveout for HorizonPay production investigation
messages:
From: ops-support@horizonpay.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.example, marcus_lin@redwood.example
Cc: security@horizonpay.com
Date: 2026-04-25T08:17:00Z
Subject: Urgent: request to preserve recent traces & transcripts for production failure (HorizonPay)

Hi Grace / Marcus,

We saw a spike of 504s around 03:40Z this morning impacting payment reconciliation for several merchants. Our SREs believe the issue requires a replay of recent inference traces and KV cache dumps tied to these request IDs: hp-req-91a, hp-req-91b, hp-req-91c.

Can Redwood temporarily suspend deletion for those request traces and associated chat transcripts for the next 5 days so our engineers can reproduce and root-cause? We understand this is an exception to your default 30-day retention and are prepared to sign any necessary attestations.

What we need from you:
- A timebound window (we proposed 5 days) where the artifacts are retained and accessible to both HorizonPay and a scoped Redwood on-call engineering pod.
- Confirmation of storage location (EU region) and that data will not be replicated outside EEA.
- Evidence of access logging/audit trail while the exception is in effect.

This is high priority for our compliance and payments teams; happy to hop on a quick call.

Thanks,
Jamie Park
Ops Support Lead, HorizonPay
attachments: HorizonPay-impact-summary.pdf (summary of merchant IDs and impacted flows)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.example
To: ops-support@horizonpay.com, marcus_lin@redwood.example
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.example
Date: 2026-04-25T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: request to preserve recent traces & transcripts for production failure (HorizonPay)

Jamie — thanks for the details and the request PDF. Marcus and I are looping in Security to scope controls and make sure the exception is timeboxed and auditable. A few clarifying questions before we escalate to approvals:

1) Exact artifact set you need: full session transcripts, model input payloads, KV cache dumps, or a filtered subset? Please call out request IDs and merchant IDs (if not in the PDF).
2) Who from HorizonPay will access the data and do they require Redwood console access or will they work via our secure SFTP pull?
3) Can HorizonPay confirm they will not export raw PII off-platform, or if they do, that it will be pseudonymized?
4) Desired retention window — you asked for 5 days; is 72 hours sufficient for an initial hold if we can extend by approval?

Action for us: I will prepare a minimal access playbook (roles, duration, logging) and share it with Security and Legal for emergency signoff. If you can answer the bullets above this morning we can try to get an approval path in the next 6-8 hours.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Escalations | Redwood Inference
redwood.example
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.example
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.example, marcus_lin@redwood.example
Date: 2026-04-25T11:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: request to preserve recent traces & transcripts for production failure (HorizonPay)

Thanks for the ping — security here. I reviewed the HorizonPay-impact-summary.pdf. We are generally open to a narrowly scoped, timeboxed exception but require the following guardrails before we can approve: 

- Scoped artifact list (only the three request IDs and associated debug logs; no broad tenant dump).
- Retention window default: 72 hours; extension to 5 days must be explicitly approved by Data Protection (me) + Legal.
- Access: only two named Redwood engineers (list required) and two named HorizonPay contacts; all access through a bastion with session recording.
- Pseudonymization: replace any customer PII in transcripts with stable hashes before any external download.
- Auditing: immutable access logs (S3/Audit bucket) within EU region; give HorizonPay access to logs for their audit.
- Deletion confirmation: automated deletion job to run at window close with a signed deletion certificate.

Please confirm who the two Redwood engineers will be and whether HorizonPay accepts the 72-hour default. If they insist on 5 days, route approval to Legal and include a brief justification of why 72 hours is insufficient (e.g., cross-team repro, third-party dependencies).

Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.example
From: marcus_lin@redwood.example
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.example, neha_kapoor@redwood.example, ops-support@horizonpay.com
Date: 2026-04-25T13:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: request to preserve recent traces & transcripts for production failure (HorizonPay)

Looping in the engineering plan. Short version: we need the artifacts for reproducing a subtle KV-cache race that only surfaces under merchant-specific traffic shapes — I expect about 2 full replay cycles to validate a fix. That said, we can minimize scope substantially. Proposed plan: 

- Scope: keep only HP request IDs hp-req-91a/b/c, associated model inputs, and KV cache keys referenced by those requests. No wholesale tenant logs.
- Access: Redwood engineers Marcus Lin (me) and Jordan Blake (cc'd on my side) will be the only Redwood users. HorizonPay nominates their engineering lead (please confirm name/email).
- Pseudonymization: we will redact cardholder-equivalent fields and replace email/phone with salted hashes before any export.
- Time window: request initial 72-hour hold. If reproduction not complete, Marcus will escalate with a short justification and we will request a one-time 48-hour extension.
- Deletion: I will run the deletion script and post the deletion certificate to the INF-4821 Jira ticket.

Attachment: repro-plan.md (high-level steps and checkpoints).

If HorizonPay agrees to the 72-hour window and the named contacts, we can start the replay within 2 hours of access being provisioned.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Staff Engineer, Runtime | Redwood Inference
attachments: repro-plan.md
